persona: Event-driven / catalyst investor. Trades attention and news flow — what's moving today/this week, winners vs losers in a group by news impact, sentiment on a name, positioning extremes (options/COT), most-talked-about names in a theme, why a stock moved, upcoming-catalyst framing. Thinks in recency windows ('this week', 'last 30 days', 'as of a date').

cases.question: What's moving in the semiconductor space this week? Give me the biggest winners and losers by news attention.
cases.goal: Surface the most news-active semiconductor names over a ~7-day window and rank them into winners vs losers by news impact/attention.
acceptance: Restricts to a recent ~1 week window, not all-time
Actually ranks/groups names into winners vs losers rather than a flat news dump
Basis for winner/loser (impact or sentiment) is grounded in real news, not asserted
If the window is genuinely thin, says so honestly instead of padding with stale items

cases.question: Why is Nvidia down today? What's the news catalyst?
cases.goal: Explain a single-name move by pointing to the actual recent news catalyst and its sentiment, or state clearly that no catalyst is found.
acceptance: Ties the move to concrete recent news items (dated), not a fabricated narrative
If no relevant catalyst exists in the news, says 'no clear news catalyst' rather than inventing one
Does not present an empty news result as 'nothing happened' if there is coverage
Sentiment/impact framing is drawn from the news, not guessed

cases.question: Give me a quick pulse on the AI theme over the last 30 days — what are the big storylines and which names are most talked about?
cases.goal: Produce a theme-level news brief for AI over a 30-day window and identify the most-mentioned/most-talked-about names.
acceptance: Honors the 30-day recency window
Surfaces the most-talked-about names by attention, not an arbitrary list
Storylines are summarized from actual news, no invented themes
Distinguishes theme-level narrative from individual stock noise

cases.question: หุ้นกลุ่มพลังงานไทยสัปดาห์นี้มีข่าวอะไรบ้าง ตัวไหนบวก ตัวไหนลบจากข่าว
cases.goal: For Thai energy stocks over the past week, list what's happening and separate names into positive vs negative by news impact.
acceptance: Scopes to Thai energy names and a ~1 week window
Splits names into positive vs negative grounded in news impact/sentiment
Replies in Thai
If coverage is sparse for Thai energy this week, states it plainly instead of fabricating

cases.question: What's the current sentiment on Tesla based on recent news? Bullish or bearish lately?
cases.goal: Give a news-grounded sentiment read on a single name over a recent window, with supporting items.
acceptance: Sentiment verdict is backed by specific recent news items
Does not fabricate a sentiment score without underlying coverage
Notes the recency window the read is based on
Acknowledges mixed/conflicting sentiment if the news is mixed

cases.question: Where is options positioning most extreme right now — any names with unusually stretched put/call or crowded positioning I should know about?
cases.goal: Surface names with positioning/options extremes (e.g. stretched put/call, crowded COT) as of now.
acceptance: Reports positioning/options extremes from actual data, not made up
Frames 'extreme' relative to a norm or range, not in isolation
If positioning data is unavailable for the ask, says so rather than inventing figures
Stays current ('right now'), not stale snapshots presented as live

cases.question: In the EV theme, which names got the most news attention over the last two weeks, and was that attention positive or negative?
cases.goal: Rank EV-theme names by news attention over a 14-day window and characterize the attention's sentiment per name.
acceptance: Honors the ~14-day window
Ranks by attention/mention volume, surfacing most-talked-about names
Pairs each name's attention with sentiment grounded in news
Does not conflate high attention with positive news

cases.question: Brief me on what happened in Japanese markets around the week of the last BOJ meeting — which sectors and names reacted the most?
cases.goal: Produce a country/market news brief for Japan anchored to a specific past date/window and identify the biggest-reacting sectors and names.
acceptance: Anchors to the specified past window (around the BOJ meeting week), not just 'latest'
Identifies which sectors/names reacted most from news impact
Does not invent a BOJ outcome or catalyst not present in the news
If the referenced window has thin coverage, is honest about it

cases.question: Between AMD, Intel and Micron — who had the better week on news? Rank them by impact.
cases.goal: Compare a small explicit set of names over the past week and rank them head-to-head by news impact/sentiment.
acceptance: Covers all three named tickers over a ~1 week window
Produces a relative ranking (winner to loser), not three separate blurbs
Ranking is justified by concrete recent news per name
Flags any name with no material news rather than padding it

cases.question: Find me any news suggesting a company might be an acquisition target or facing a regulatory investigation recently — the kind of catalyst-driven stuff worth watching.
cases.goal: Do a semantic news search for catalyst-shaped events (M&A target, regulatory probe) over a recent window and return grounded hits.
acceptance: Returns news items that actually match the catalyst intent (M&A / regulatory), semantically not just keyword
Items are recent and dated
Does not invent M&A rumors or investigations absent from the news
If nothing matches, says so instead of forcing weak hits
